paper-64gib.label: 64 GiB paper configuration
paper-64gib.note: FACE Case 5 provides 64 GiB of local HBM per NPU in the paper configuration.

validation-160gib.label: 160 GiB validation extension
validation-160gib.note: Validation-only capacity extension for workloads that require 160 GiB of local HBM per NPU. Only reachable under the legacy compute node; the die node's capacity-alignment check rejects it.

validation-die-64g.label: 64 GB die-aligned validation profile
validation-die-64g.note: Bytes exactly equal to the die-derived HBM capacity (hbm-sides x hbm-per-side x 16 GiB); config_resolver hard-checks the alignment when the hardware die node is present (contract section 3.4).

validation-coarse-144g.label: 144 GB coarse_die_v2 die-derived capacity
validation-coarse-144g.note: coarse_die_v2 backend aligned: exactly 2 rows x 2 stacks x 36 GB per die

notes: The physical mesh is row-major with 9 rows and 6 columns.
The analytical network lists dimensions as columns then rows.

The die node replaces the legacy compute.peak-perf-tflops description (mutually exclusive, contract section 3.1): large cores / 0.75 MB SRAM per core / 800 mm2 compute area / HBM 4 stacks on one side / 512-bit die NoC. Derived: 35x35 = 1225 cores, 1492.05 TFLOPS PE peak, 1640 GB/s (strictly continuous with the former 1640 GB/s local-hbm bandwidth), 64 GB HBM capacity.
D2D latency is modeled as a per-hop adjacent-link latency.
The remote-memory pool is attached to every physical mesh-boundary NPU.
The 512 GB/s remote-memory bandwidth and 100 ns latency are shared simulator assumptions.
The capacity profile describes local HBM placement per NPU.

User-authorized engineering comparison point (2026-10-16), materialized in the architecture block 2026-10-19 through 2026-10-20 (while active it was key-for-key equal to die/configs/tx8_compute_matched_hardware.json in template_newdie; since 2026-10-21 that file alone carries it): 10 x 10 Core grid on a 25 mm x 32 mm compute Die, 0.75 MiB SRAM/Core and 512-bit NoC. The derived architectural PE peak of this configuration is 126.6 INT4 TOPS, numerically compared with the TX8 128 BF16 TFLOPS reference; precision and independent measurement are not equivalent (calibration_status stays assumed; all eta/kappa/launch values are engineering priors). Derived Vec FP32-equivalent peak is 12.65728 T eq-op/s, not the TX8 1 T reference. HBM stays 2 rows x 2 stacks x 36 GB = 144 GB per die at 4710.4 GB/s aggregate (the legacy 4 x 16 GB / 410 GB/s per-stack reference of the top-level local-hbm bandwidth entry is the preserved non-die base, not this coarse block).
Default die backend is coarse_die_v2: the coarse-die descriptor above is resolved by the coarse library; the 144 GB validation capacity profile matches its derived per-die HBM capacity exactly.

2026-10-21 wafer-fit default redesign (user-directed): the checked-in coarse-die architecture block is now the maximum compute Die that still fits the 9x6 die mesh inside the 215x215 mm system region under the legacy 10% interconnect reserve (effective extent = outline/sqrt(0.9)): die 33.99448 x 22.66298 mm = 770.416 mm2 (215*sqrt(0.9)/6 by 215*sqrt(0.9)/9, five-decimal truncation inward), 13x9 Core grid (117 Cores), 1.5 MiB SRAM/Core, 256-bit NoC; architectural peaks 833.04 INT4 TOPS and 83.300724 Vec FP32-eq TFLOPS per die (best >=256-bit row of the 32-row table at this outline). The prior 25x32 mm / 10x10 / 0.75 MiB / 512-bit block could not host the 9-row direction of the mesh (9x32=288>215 even at zero reserve; only 6 rows at the 10% reserve) and remains verbatim in die/configs/tx8_compute_matched_hardware.json, which keeps its 2026-10-16 authorization and numbers. HBM stays 2 rows x 2 stacks x 36 GB = 144 GB per die at 4710.4 GB/s (validation-coarse-144g unchanged); the bump budget at 770.416 mm2 (~31,835 GB/s) still covers HBM plus the 4050 GB/s D2D links. The wafer array counts the compute Die outline; the two-row co-planar HBM module outline (34.29 x 45.22 mm) is a packaging-layer diagnostic and does not gate the wafer mesh.
